description.purpose: Context assembly as a hive: the orchestrator that decides what enters an LLM's context window and what leaves it. A rolling short-term conversation window (user and assistant turns, session-scoped, store-backed), the memory bundle, the tool round fanned back in, and a cap over every one of those three legs that is deterministic configuration rather than a model judgement. Everything the brain sees leaves through ONE message on one route - and the same seam ends a runaway tool round and hands a closed session on as one batch, so a later split of the agent behind that seam does not re-cut the collector. A round that loses a tool result exits deterministically past an idle window (synthetic error results, round_stale=1), and a user turn arriving mid-round defers instead of opening a second brain call - decided behaviour where there used to be accident. Since 1.1.0 the window is also CURATED: a budget projection that runs at every assembly - not at a threshold - and replaces tool payloads it cannot afford with stubs that carry a recovery key, in declared stages, without a single model call. What it may take is declared per tool name; everything undeclared is unique and is never touched, so an undeclared tool costs context and never correctness. Since 3.1.0 the curator sees the WHOLE projection (GH #451) - the rounds, the window, `system.*` as a tree and the tool declarations as an array - and the tool block counts towards the budget, which it never did although it is the largest block in a real prompt. Two further stages follow from that: a declaration whose tool went unused for `keep_rounds` iterations is stubbed to its name and one line, recoverable with `thread_recall(call_id="tool:<name>")`, and an over-size `system.*` slot of the collector's own making is cut to its head. The generator is also TOLD where it stands: one deterministic sentence in `system.budget` naming tokens used and tokens left. The conversation, the protected `system.*` families - instructions, identity, persona, handover - the tool_call names, the newest rounds and every tool in use are out of reach at every stage, which is why the same question has the same answer basis before and after any number of curations - the property a prose fold cannot have, because this one rewrites no text at all. `thread_recall` is the way back: the collector serves it itself, out of its own slate, uncapped, behind a per-turn budget wall. Housekeeping is evidence-gated: the close batch writes a delivery ledger row, and only ledger-named, aged sessions are ever pruned - on an operator lane the template never fires itself. Since 3.2.0 ([#458](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/458)) it also carries the ONE lane through which durable state reaches the brain from outside: `in_pack`. The agent composites this hive stands in are sealed, so every path from outside to their brain runs through this cell, and an identity had no entrance at all until this lane existed -- `affinity` could push and there was nowhere to push to. What may be written is a closed list (`identity`, `persona`, `handover`, `instructions`), a subset of the curator's `SYS_KEEP` minus the two families this cell re-derives itself. `instructions` was a third subtraction until [#488](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/488): withholding the charter assumed it had another owner, and it had none -- nothing exported it, no template seeded it, and a grown generation came up with an empty charter and answered as the vendor's default assistant, so it joins the lane and is guarded by the edge that stamps the lane rather than by being unwritable; an unknown slot refuses the whole pack rather than writing the half it understood. A new accepted lane and two new emitted ones is the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a) -- nothing that shipped changed behaviour. Since 3.3.0 ([#464](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/464)) the tool menu is ASKED FOR instead of typed: `params.tools` is the list of names the agent's own template says it uses, a tick on `in_menu_tick` sends exactly those names to the tools hive, and the answer comes back on `in_menu` and leaves on `menu` as durable `system.tools` in the brain -- one write, not a per-turn cost, and the same durable place `pack` writes to. `tool_menu` stays as the manual override and switches the asking off, because two writers on one slot path would overwrite each other every round; a declared name the hive has nothing under comes back in `hop.menu_unknown` and as a warn line, never as a silence. Two accepted lanes and two emitted ones is the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a) -- nothing that shipped changed behaviour, and a collector that declares no tools behaves exactly as 3.2.0 did. Since 3.3.1 ([#512](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/512)) that menu also keeps the two tools this hive answers ITSELF. `memory_recall` is served out of its own recall port and `thread_recall` out of its own slate, no tools hive has a declaration for either, and they shipped as SEED rows in the brain's `cell.db` -- written once at birth and replaced whole by the first tick, because the menu write is a `$replace`. A grown agent therefore lost its memory tool minutes into its life while the entire recall chain below it stayed wired and idle. The declarations belong to the cell that answers the calls; which of the two a given collector declares is decided by the switch that already decides whether the lane is answered instead of refused (`thread_recall`), so there is no new knob. `memory_recall` stood beside it until 4.0.0 and is the memory hive's own declaration since GH #552. Added after the empty-menu guard and never over a name the hive itself answered. A repair is the third digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a). Since 3.4.0 ([#529](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/529)) that menu is a UNION over ANSWERERS instead of one answer. Before it, one reply WAS the menu -- parse, add the self-served names, write the lot with `$replace` -- which is right while exactly one thing answers and is the whole defect the moment two do: the second reply would not merge with the first, it would delete it, and the two would take the menu away from each other on every tick forever. A second answerer is now required, because a tool the composite reaches by an edge on its NAME is topology of the level that draws the edge and only the side that ANSWERS it can declare it. So each answerer's last submenu is kept as one row of this hive's own store, keyed by `context.tool_answerer` -- the mirror of the `tool_caller` the request already carries -- and every answer re-derives the menu from all the rows, ordered by answerer so the same rows always produce the same menu. An answer with no answerer on it is the one-answerer shape and counts as the default one, so a tree wired before this behaves exactly as it did. Two consequences fall out: `menu_unknown` is computed against the MERGED menu, so a name one answerer has nothing under but another delivers is not a finding; and a store that refuses the merge is a warn line and a stop rather than a `degraded` answer, because a menu is durable state with no turn beside it and the next tick asks again. A second store table and a new phase is the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a) -- nothing a caller sends or receives changed shape. Since 3.5.0 a round that spends its ITERATION budget ends on a named PARTIAL ANSWER instead of on the raw end of the tool round (GH #570): the seam appends one assistant text turn saying which bound it hit, how many calls it made, which tools it called and the head of the last result, and stamps `hop.partial`. What a consumer reads is the LAST text of an answer, so a capped round used to hand a surface a raw tool payload and the person was shown a search dump -- the better the errand was going, the more certainly a tool got quoted at the reader. The raw round is untouched and still in the `round` table, reachable by `thread_recall`. `hop.partial` is the marker `round_capped` could never be: that key means the round ended early OR that some bytes were trimmed off a round still going, and only the first is an answer somebody is looking at. A new hop key and a text promise nothing made before is the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a). Since 4.0.0 the ask has a CAUSE instead of a cadence (GH #553): the hive accepts `mutation_committed` -- the mutation door's receipt, carried in by the level above -- and its own door turns it into the internal `in_menu_tick` the `./menu-clock` timer used to stamp. The timer is gone; the boot receipt is the first ask, so an agent has its menu before its first turn, and a tool added by mutation reaches it with the receipt of that very mutation. Since 1.2.0 every knob of this cell is a PARAM read off the stdin document rather than a `COLLECTOR_*` substitution token out of the colony's environment ([#138](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/138)), and this template is the REFERENCE migration for the move: two collectors in one colony are tuned apart without a fork of the script, and there is no environment fallback left to read.
description.use_when: One per agent brain, between the inbound surface and the LLM. It replaces the pattern where a persona cell injects the system prompt, a prep cell mints the turn id and a third cell fans tool results in: those are one concern and this is it. Wire the entry lanes and the exit routes in the SAME mutation that instantiates it - an island without a crossing edge stays inactive.
description.not_in_scope: No inference and no persona (identity is not context assembly). No tool fan-OUT: routing a tool_call to the right tool stays a dispatcher's job, the collector only fans the results back in - including the one tool it serves itself, memory_recall, which reaches it over an ordinary tool edge the dispatcher chose by name (GH #78). No session lifecycle: a keeper decides when a generation begins and ends, the collector consumes the session_id and answers the close request. No memory judgement: the collector READS the recall bundle and hands a closed session on unfiltered, but what is extracted and what is kept belongs to the receiver of the write batch. No LLM judgement anywhere - every cap is a number. No cap deletes: every cut is a read-time cut and the full value stays in the store; rows fall only on the in_prune lane, only for sessions whose close batch already left (the batched ledger row is the evidence) and only behind params.prune_after_ms - without that evidence the store grows rather than loses a turn, and the collector never schedules a prune itself. No second body format for a tool result: a result is the `tool_result` turns of its `messages[]` and nothing else. A `system` slot on the in_tool lane is dropped, and that is not an oversight (GH #252): `system.*` leaving the seam is upserted into the brain cell's own cell.db and outlives the round that wrote it, so nothing that is the evidence of ONE round belongs there. Since 2.1.0 that rule has no exception left - the memory bundle was the one carve-out and does not live in system.* either any more, it arrives as a synthetic memory_recall tool result inside the round it was fetched for, and what stays under system.memory is the revocation of that slot (GH #278). And `in_pack` is not a general write channel into the prompt: it is four slot names, checked against a constant, with the owner taken off the envelope. WHO may open such a lane is not this cell's question either -- the edge that opens it is a mutation, and `templates/submit` asks the broker for the capability while checking the edge's own form itself (GH #458).
examples: PORTS - every endpoint is the HIVE path (`params.ports` is empty since GH #228; an edge naming ./assemble or ./window is refused with hive_port_boundary), and what a caller wants rides on hop.route. Entry (the parent edge names the lane via set_hop route and promotes session_id): in_turn (an inbound user turn), in_bundle (the memory hive's recall bundle), in_advice (an advisor core's answer, arriving after its turn ended), in_calls (the assistant tool_call turn from a dispatcher), in_tool (one tool result: every turn of its messages[], filed under the call id each turn answers -- a result that answers two calls in one message closes both, and a `system` slot or a top-level body slot on a result is dropped at the lane on purpose, GH #252), in_thread_call (a thread_recall tool_call, likewise served here - it brings a payload the curator elided back out of THIS turn's own round table), in_answer (the brain's final turn), in_close (a session keeper's close request, hop.route == 'close'), in_prune (a timer's or operator's housekeeping request, hop.route == 'prune'), in_round_sweep (a timer's or operator's stuck-round re-check, hop.route == 'sweep'). Exit (from the hive path, on hop.route): 'brain' -> the agent LLM (promote hop.iter and hop.turn_id to context on that edge), 'answer' -> the reply sink, 'recall' -> the memory hive's recall port (the per-turn leg when params.memory_tier is set, and every memory_recall call; promote recall_query / memory_tier / memory_call_id / recall_window_from / recall_window_to / session_id / turn_id / iter), 'write' -> wherever a closed session belongs, 'turn_write' -> a memory hive's episode lane, ONE message per turn and never a batch (GH #298, ruling Q11): after every stored turn and every stored answer, every turn of the session not yet written leaves as its own message - one user/assistant turn in messages[], hop.turn_id '<session_id>#<index>', hop.turn_index and hop.happened_at beside it - so an episode exists at the turn instead of at the close. On by default; params.turn_write '' or '0' switches it off, and off means the conversation reaches no memory at all. Do NOT wire 'write' into the same consumer: that route carries a closed day with its rounds slot, and a second edge into the same memory would be a second writer over turns this lane already wrote, 'prune' -> a log sink or the operator surface (one report per pruned session).
turn 3 of a session references turn 1: the window carries turns 1..3 into the context, so the answer does not depend on retrieval luck

params.window_turns=5 over a 40-turn session: the store returns the 5 newest, hop.window_capped=1; a byte cap that cannot afford the oldest of them drops it and everything older, hop.window_dropped counts them
2 parallel tool calls: 1 assistant row + 2 tool rows in the round table, the guarded update wins once, and the re-entry carries the window AND the tool round through the same seam
a tool that answers two calls in ONE message: both results are filed under their own tool_call_id, the round is complete and fires -- the lane keeps the whole messages[], not its first turn
a 100 KB tool result: params.tool_chars of it reach the seam with hop.round_capped=1, all of it stays readable in the round table
a model that will not stop asking for tools: at params.max_iter the seam emits route 'answer' with what it collected instead of a further brain call
the keeper closes a generation: one message on route 'write' with every turn of the session in order and every round row beside it, and the delivery ledger row written in the same multi-send

a timer fires the prune lane a week later: the delivered session's rows fall up to its close boundary, the living session keeps every byte, and the cut is reported on route 'prune' - without a ledger row the same request cuts nothing and says so

a tool dies mid-flight and one result never arrives: the round parks, and the next turn, the next result or an in_round_sweep request after params.round_idle_ms closes it - the missing call is answered synthetically under its own tool_call_id and the round fires with round_stale=1
a user turn lands while a round is running: it enters the window, defers (no second brain call on the session), and rides with the next regular assembly marked round_deferred=1

a tool loop over twenty large file reads: the curator elides the payloads of the declared-recoverable ones from every round older than params.keep_rounds, leaves a stub with a content hash and a thread_recall key in their place, and reports hop.curate_stage / hop.curate_elided / hop.curate_saved - no model was asked and no word was rewritten

the model needs an elided result back: it calls thread_recall(call_id) and gets the ORIGINAL text, uncapped, as a tool_result of the running round - over params.thread_recall_budget the call is refused with a typed error instead of being silently halved

the model wants memory about a TIME RANGE: it emits a memory_recall tool_call, the dispatcher routes it by hop.tool_name like any other tool, and the collector - which already owns the recall port - serves the call itself, passes the window on as recall_window_from/_to and answers under the original tool_call_id, so the round ends where it began (GH #78)

a tool menu the collector owns (params.tool_menu): the declarations travel as system.tools with $replace on every assembly, they count towards the budget, and the ones nobody called inside params.keep_rounds leave as name + one line of description - hop.curate_tools counts them, and thread_recall(call_id="tool:<name>") hands the schema straight back out of the menu, with no store read
